## TL;DR

The Model providers tab now lists Muse with live subscription-allowance figures pulled from the machine's own `muse login` session via `muse usage --json`, rendered with the same rolling-window percent bars as opencode Go plus a plan hero. When the session is missing or unreadable the row degrades to a retryable error with the dashboard/docs link still one click away. A chip row at the top of the page jumps to any provider section with a smooth scroll and flash, following the Settings General tab's section nav.

## Work and rationale

Muse is a functional headless agent in this repo (`muse exec --json`, UUID sessions) but had no row in `MODEL_PROVIDERS`, so the tab undercounted the agents users actually run. The task asked for automatic usage/subscription details following the opencode Go pattern where applicable, with a link fallback, plus top-of-page provider navigation following the Settings General tab.

Probing the installed CLI showed `muse usage --json` emits a machine-readable allowance object (`tier`, `window`/`weekly` with `usedPercent` and `resetsAtMs`, `asOfMs`), so a live integration was possible without inventing a data source. The allowance maps cleanly onto the opencode Go window shape — label, percent, reset — minus dollars, which Muse never reports, exactly like Go's "no dollar balance exists" note. Key design decisions:

- New `muse` entry in `MODEL_PROVIDERS` (`src/core/providers/spend.ts`) as `kind: "live"` with `envVar`/`configKey` null, dashboard URL `https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code` (the verified official URL already recorded in `agent-compatibility.json`). Live-kind keeps the "live" pill and the usage pipeline; null key fields mark it as login-backed.
- New `usesCliLogin` flag on the list endpoint, derived as `kind === "live" && envVar == null`, so the UI can tell "paste a key" rows from "reads the harness login" rows without hardcoding provider ids.
- Server `GET /api/model-providers/muse/usage` spawns `muse usage --json` with an 8s timeout, parses with a tolerant `parseMuseUsage` (unknown window-shaped keys accepted, bare cost objects rejected — the same rule as the Go parser), and throws actionable errors the route maps to 502: missing binary, timeout, logged-out session (exit 0 with empty stdout, hint on stderr), and unrecognized shapes with a `reason`/`hint`.
- `POST .../muse/key` refuses with a message pointing at `muse login`, since there is nothing to store.
- The panel renders the Muse tier as a hero and the windows with the existing percent-bar markup via a shared `windowedUsage` helper; CLI-login rows show a login hint instead of the key form and get Refresh-only actions. A provider chip nav (`aria-label="Model providers"`, active chip, smooth scroll, flash ring, reduced-motion guard) mirrors the Settings section chips.
- `user-docs/agents.md` updated to mention Muse in the tab description.

## Approaches tried

Link-only row first: with no verified usage source, the task explicitly blesses a dashboard link-out, and that was the initial plan — a `kind: "link"` Muse entry plus the nav. Before settling there I probed the installed CLI (`muse usage --help`, then `muse usage --json` against the live session and against an empty HOME to simulate logged-out). Both shapes were clean and stable, so I upgraded to the live integration: the acceptance criterion prefers pulled-in details "where available", and here they were available with no secret handling at all.

For the row kind I considered a third `kind` value (e.g. `"harness"`) but rejected it: it would ripple through `ModelProviderKind`, every pill/Form branch, and all fixtures. Null key fields on a live row plus one boolean flag carried the distinction with far less surface.

For the nav I considered wiring a `?section=`-style URL param like Settings, but the panel lives inside AgentsView's tab query and owns no route of its own; local active-chip state plus anchor scroll delivers the same UX without coupling to the router.

## Challenges and blockers

- The logged-out `muse usage --json` exits 0 with empty stdout and the hint on stderr, so the fetcher cannot rely on exit codes — it must treat unparseable stdout as the failure path and surface stderr. Verified by running with an empty HOME rather than touching the real login.
- `parseMuseUsage` tolerates ratio-vs-percent ambiguity (`<= 1` treated as a ratio) the same way the Go parser does, since the endpoint has no published schema and a future `0.18`-style value should not render as 0%.
- One pre-existing panel test addressed the Copilot row by positional index, which shifted when Muse was inserted after Codex; updated the index rather than the expectation. No other suites enumerate the registry.
- No human-gated blockers: the only environment-dependent behavior (presence of a `muse login` session) degrades to the specified link-out plus a retryable error, which the new tests pin.

## Key learnings

- `muse usage --json` is the machine-readable allowance source for the local session: `{ allowance: { tier, window: { usedPercent, resetsAtMs }, weekly, ... }, reason, hint }`. Logged-out produces exit 0, empty stdout, and `muse usage: not logged in: run \`muse login\` first` on stderr.
- The provider tab's live/keyed distinction is really "live data via pasted key" vs "live data via harness login" vs "link-out"; encoding that as `usesCliLogin` keeps the registry as the single source of truth and the UI data-driven.
- The opencode Go window rendering (label, percent bar, reset line) generalizes to any allowance-shaped provider by leaving the dollar fields null — future login-backed providers can reuse the same block.
